A.explanation: This uses $\tan\theta = 0.10/0.12$. It inverts the $x$ and $y$ momenta and gives the angle to the $y$-direction.

B.explanation: This is about $40^{\circ}$, the complement of the correct angle. It finds $\tan^{-1}(0.10/0.12)$ instead of $\tan^{-1}(0.12/0.10)$.

C.explanation: With $p_x = 0.10$ and $p_y = 0.12$ in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$, $\tan\theta = 0.12/0.10 = 1.2$ gives $\theta \approx 50^{\circ}$.

D.explanation: This is $1^{\circ}$ too large and does not follow from $\tan^{-1}(1.2) \approx 50.2^{\circ}$ with the given $0.20 \text{ kg}$, $0.30 \text{ kg}$, $0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $0.40 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Notice the collision is two-dimensional: the $0.20 \text{ kg}$ ball brings only $x$-momentum and the $0.30 \text{ kg}$ ball brings only $y$-momentum.
Recall momentum is conserved separately in $x$ and $y$, so the stuck-together mass must carry $p_x = 0.20 \times 0.50$ and $p_y = 0.30 \times 0.40$.
Connect the direction $\theta$ to those components with $\tan\theta = p_y/p_x$, then evaluate $0.12/0.10$ before taking $\tan^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify the initial momenta from the diagram. In $x$: $p_x = m_1 u_1 = 0.20 \times 0.50 = 0.10 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$. In $y$: $p_y = m_2 u_2 = 0.30 \times 0.40 = 0.12 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.

Apply conservation of momentum separately in each direction. Because the balls stick together, the combined mass $(0.20 + 0.30) \text{ kg}$ must have these same $x$ and $y$ components of momentum after collision.
Relate the final direction $\theta$ measured from the $x$-direction to the components. The momentum vector forms a right-angled triangle, so $\tan\theta = p_y/p_x$.
Calculate the angle: $\theta = \tan^{-1}(1.2) \approx 50.2^{\circ}$, which to the given options is $50^{\circ}$. This is option C.
